bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Debt-free company with high cash reserves and strong financial performance" is stated as a key strength and repeated as "A debt-free company with a high cash reserve demonstrating strong financial stability and growth potential."
- Net Debt (INR Cr.) is shown negative across the period: -41 (FY23), -48 (FY24), -182 (FY25), -66 (FY26); the FY26 balance sheet shows non-current borrowings of 0.0 and current borrowings of 15.0.
- Returns as printed: RoCE 26.80% / 25.80% / 18.83% / 21.26% and RoE 20.40% / 19.40% / 14.35% / 15.27% for FY23 / FY24 / FY25 / FY26.
- Cash conversion turned negative in FY26: "Net Cash from Operating Activities" of -18.8 (vs 53.6 in FY25, 81.5 in FY24), driven by "Changes in working capital" of -164.6, with trade receivables (current) rising to 288.2 and non-current trade receivables to 111.0.
- The MD commits to "disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation and continuous operational improvement"; the deck states no dividend, payout or buyback policy anywhere.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated model covering estimation, detailed engineering, structural design, fabrication, on-site installation and erection in-house, giving greater quality control, faster turnaround and execution coordination
- Second-largest integrated PEB player in India with a 6.5% market share (source: CRISIL)
- Debt-free and financially resilient with strong reserves, enabling self-funding of expansion plans
- Long-standing customer relationships — three of the top five customer groups have stayed with the Company for more than five years
- Proprietary IBSL K-Series automation platform linking STAAD and Tekla systems, sharply cutting fabrication-drawing turnaround time
- Digital integration via SAP S/4HANA rollout and growing use of AI in engineering and project management
- Deepening presence in specialised high-value verticals (semiconductor, EV, data centres, renewable energy) requiring specialised precision engineering
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Industry and macro risk — exposure to economic cycles, infrastructure demand and competitive pricing pressure — The Company remains exposed to economic cycles, infrastructure demand and competitive pricing pressures; geopolitical tensions across regions like the Middle East and Europe continue to disrupt freight movement and supply chains, and the increasing scale of operations heightens sensitivity to market fluctuations.
- Price and supply-chain risk — raw material and global supply-chain volatility — Volatility in raw material prices and global supply chains can impact procurement costs, margins, and project execution timelines; dependence on international trade movements increases exposure to pricing fluctuations and supply disruptions.
- Design and engineering risk — rising complexity of multi-storey and heavy steel structures — Rising complexity in multi-storey and heavy steel structures increases execution risk; errors at the design stage can cause structural failures, rework, delays, and higher financial and reputational impact given larger project sizes.
- Environmental and regulatory risk — tightening sustainability regulation — Regulatory focus on sustainability continues to increase, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements under upcoming waste management rules effective April 2026; projects are also subject to environmental certification requirements such as LEED and IGBC standards.
- Safety and operational risk — hazards across an expanding multi-plant manufacturing footprint — Expansion across five manufacturing facilities and continuous operations increase exposure to workplace hazards, including electrical, fire, and heavy-material-handling risks; compliance with ISO 45001:2018 remains critical, especially for green building projects.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Ranked among integrated PEB players in India in FY25: 2nd", with "Market share among integrated PEB players in India: 6.5%" and "Presence in the PEB and Building Products Industry: 40+ Years".
- Six listed key strengths: integrated manufacturing backed by in-house design/engineering and on-site project management; market position and brand presence; execution track record; diverse customer base with long-standing relationships; experienced promoters and management; and "Debt-free company with high cash reserves and strong financial performance."
- Scale of delivery: "850+ Completed execution of PEB Contracts from FY15 to FY26", with projects cited across an airport (Delhi), a data centre (Navi Mumbai), solar PV module plants (Dholera and Jaipur), hospitals, food processing and industrial & logistics parks.
- Industry structure favours the company's cohort: organised players are 40-45% of the Indian PEB market with top 6 players at 80-85% of the organised segment, and FY19-23 CAGR of 11.4% for Top 6 Players vs 8.5% Total Industry and 7.0% Rest of the Industry (Source: Prospectus).
- Customer stickiness: "3 of 5 Customer Groups have been associated for over five years" and repeat orders were 72% of revenue from operations in FY26 (80% FY23, 81% FY24, 82% FY25).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] "Total Order book as on 31st July 2026, is INR 1,864 Cr", with "Order Wins (Rs in Crs) 609" for "Orders booked between 01st May 2026 and 31st July 2026" and a "major order worth Rs. 165 crore in Gujarat" secured during the quarter. The order-book pie prints 30% and 70% against an "Industrial / Infrastructure" legend, but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from the extract, so the split is not asserted here.
- [JV] Joint Venture Agreement with ER Steel Inc, Canada — Interarch 76% / ER Steel 24% — "to establish a structured framework for jointly evaluating the design, engineering, manufacturing and supply of OWSJ products through a scalable and cost-efficient platform in India". Interarch leads engineering, detailing, manufacturing and quality compliance from India; ER Steel supports market development and sales in USA & Canada.
- [JV terms] "Total funding required by the JV company to procure land, to undertake the development and operationalization of the Business is expected to be INR 80 Crs", and "ER Steel must enter into 100% Offtake Agreement with the JV Co and purchase the total quantity of OWSJ products for distribution and sale in Canada & USA. This is a major commercial assurance for the JV."
- [Export tie-up] Collaboration with Mold-Tek Technologies Limited (MTTL): Interarch handles manufacturing and logistics while MTTL provides detailing for PEB and structural steel projects; a "two-year business plan, extendable by mutual consent", exclusivity "on projects introduced by MTTL", and Interarch pays MTTL "a commission on export orders generated through MTTL's efforts".
- [Export certifications] "Certificate for Inspection Program for Manufacturer of Metal Building System issued by IAS used to supply the pre-engineered buildings in USA" and an "International Code Council – Certificate issued to supply LGFS products in the USA".
- [Name change / one-off] The company is "Formerly known as Interarch Building Products Limited"; FY26 carries an Exceptional Item of -3.2 footnoted as a "One time statutory impact of new Labour Codes".

business.body: Interarch manufactures, supplies, erects and installs pre-engineered building (PEB) systems and related metal products, running the full project life-cycle in-house from estimation, detailed engineering and structural design through fabrication, on-site installation and erection. outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Moving beyond industrial infrastructure into higher-value, more complex steel construction work such as multi-storey commercial buildings, hospitals, airports and government projects.
- Expanding into Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) to widen the addressable market and participate in large-scale infrastructure/industrial projects beyond core PEB.
- Building a strong export business as a strategic objective — deepening North American presence via a strategic understanding with ER Steel INC. and an international-business-development association with Mold-Tek Technologies Limited, while pursuing further expansion into markets such as the Middle East.
- Long-term vision to be a leading provider of light, medium and heavy steel building solutions across diverse sectors — manufacturing facilities, heavy-load data centres, steel plants, high-rise commercial/institutional buildings, shopping malls, stadiums, ports and power plants.
- Pursuing growth with financial discipline, leveraging a net cash-positive balance sheet, strong reserves and prudent working-capital management to self-fund expansion.
- Deepening presence in emerging high-value sectors — data centres, renewable energy/solar power, semiconductor manufacturing, and EV/lithium-battery ecosystems — viewed as key future growth drivers.
- Continued focus on operational excellence and technology (automation, procurement optimisation, operating leverage) to protect profitability while scaling.
- Gujarat manufacturing facility marks the Company's first production base in Western India, intended to improve delivery timelines and logistics efficiency and to help it compete more effectively in the price-sensitive mid-sized project segment in Gujarat/Maharashtra, historically among its largest markets.
- The Company pursues growth with financial discipline, describing itself as debt-free and net cash-positive with strong reserves, which it says leaves it well positioned to self-fund expansion plans while retaining the agility to invest in future-ready capabilities. Prudent working-capital management is cited as giving room to invest with confidence while staying financially resilient. Consistent with this, the Board has recommended a final dividend for FY 2025-26 for Members' approval at the AGM, continuing the Company's practice of returning dividends to shareholders alongside self-funded reinvestment in capacity.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26 Interarch commissioned Phase II of its Athivaram (Andhra Pradesh) PEB facility and a third production line at Kichha (both operational since September 2025), plus a new automated box column line in Uttarakhand, taking total PEB capacity to 2,01,000 MTPA. The Company also commenced construction of two strategically important projects: a new PEB manufacturing facility in Gujarat (its first production base in Western India, targeting the Gujarat/Maharashtra markets) and a Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh. Gujarat Phase I commenced operations in July 2026 and Phase II is expected to be completed before December 2026; land has already been acquired for a sixth, fully integrated Gujarat plant expected to begin production by FY 2027-28. The dedicated Athivaram HSS facility is being commissioned in August 2026 and is expected to be commercialised by FY 2026-27, with HSS capacity targeted at 60,000 MT by 2027 and combined PEB+HSS installed capacity targeted at 2,65,000 MT by Q3 FY 2026-27; Phase II of the Andhra Pradesh HSS project has already commenced, targeted operational in H1 2027, and the Company holds sufficient land for a future Phase III. This expansion is funded in part by a INR 100 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) initiated to double heavy steel structure capacity and support a targeted revenue milestone of INR 2,500 crore by FY 2027-28. Capacity growth has been matched by manufacturing automation (3-axis drilling, automated cutting of complex steel sections) that has reduced workforce requirements by more than half in affected processes. As of March 2026 the order book stood at INR 1,552 crore, supported by rising demand from data centres and semiconductor facilities and the Company's first major export orders from Ghana and Myanmar.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- PEB demand is driven by rising investment in manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, data centres, industrial parks and infrastructure development.
- The industrial sector (automobiles, cement, oil & gas and other core industries) remains the anchor for PEB adoption, while infrastructure applications — warehouses, cold storage, data centres, power plants, aircraft hangars, railway infrastructure — are emerging as the market's next significant growth frontier.
- Organised players hold a structural advantage over the unorganised segment in executing large-scale, time-sensitive projects, reinforcing the case for scaled, integrated manufacturers.
- Steel is increasingly becoming the preferred construction material worldwide owing to its strength, speed of construction, sustainability and cost efficiency.
- Government initiatives — PLI schemes, Make in India, semiconductor manufacturing, renewable energy, electric vehicles, battery manufacturing and data-centre development — are expected to generate significant demand for PEB and structural-steel solutions.
- FY26 revenue growth was driven by rising demand, an improving project mix with a greater share of high-value industrial and manufacturing projects, and execution capability enabled by the expanded manufacturing footprint.
- Rising demand is being seen from leading domestic and global corporations for marquee projects in renewable energy, solar power and data centres, which management expects to remain key growth drivers in the years ahead.
- Closed FY 2025-26 with an order book exceeding INR 1,552 crore.
- Executed the largest single Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) order in the Company's history during FY26.
- Secured major new orders during FY26 from marquee customers including Ather, Ascendas, Rungta Mines, Tata Jaguar, Tecno Data Centre, Takenaka, World Green Energy, JSW JFE, Indo Asia Copper, Bhuwaneshwari Foods & Beverages and CESC Green Power, many partnering with the Company for the first time.

currentContext.expansion: During FY26 Interarch commissioned Phase II of its Athivaram (Andhra Pradesh) PEB facility and a third production line at Kichha (both operational since September 2025), plus a new automated box column line in Uttarakhand, taking total PEB capacity to 2,01,000 MTPA. The Company also commenced construction of two strategically important projects: a new PEB manufacturing facility in Gujarat (its first production base in Western India, targeting the Gujarat/Maharashtra markets) and a Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh. Gujarat Phase I commenced operations in July 2026 and Phase II is expected to be completed before December 2026; land has already been acquired for a sixth, fully integrated Gujarat plant expected to begin production by FY 2027-28. The dedicated Athivaram HSS facility is being commissioned in August 2026 and is expected to be commercialised by FY 2026-27, with HSS capacity targeted at 60,000 MT by 2027 and combined PEB+HSS installed capacity targeted at 2,65,000 MT by Q3 FY 2026-27; Phase II of the Andhra Pradesh HSS project has already commenced, targeted operational in H1 2027, and the Company holds sufficient land for a future Phase III. This expansion is funded in part by a INR 100 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) initiated to double heavy steel structure capacity and support a targeted revenue milestone of INR 2,500 crore by FY 2027-28. Capacity growth has been matched by manufacturing automation (3-axis drilling, automated cutting of complex steel sections) that has reduced workforce requirements by more than half in affected processes. As of March 2026 the order book stood at INR 1,552 crore, supported by rising demand from data centres and semiconductor facilities and the Company's first major export orders from Ghana and Myanmar.

risks.risk: Industry and macro risk — exposure to economic cycles, infrastructure demand and competitive pricing pressure
risks.note: The Company remains exposed to economic cycles, infrastructure demand and competitive pricing pressures; geopolitical tensions across regions like the Middle East and Europe continue to disrupt freight movement and supply chains, and the increasing scale of operations heightens sensitivity to market fluctuations.

risks.risk: Price and supply-chain risk — raw material and global supply-chain volatility
risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices and global supply chains can impact procurement costs, margins, and project execution timelines; dependence on international trade movements increases exposure to pricing fluctuations and supply disruptions.

risks.risk: Design and engineering risk — rising complexity of multi-storey and heavy steel structures
risks.note: Rising complexity in multi-storey and heavy steel structures increases execution risk; errors at the design stage can cause structural failures, rework, delays, and higher financial and reputational impact given larger project sizes.

risks.risk: Environmental and regulatory risk — tightening sustainability regulation
risks.note: Regulatory focus on sustainability continues to increase, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements under upcoming waste management rules effective April 2026; projects are also subject to environmental certification requirements such as LEED and IGBC standards.

risks.risk: Safety and operational risk — hazards across an expanding multi-plant manufacturing footprint
risks.note: Expansion across five manufacturing facilities and continuous operations increase exposure to workplace hazards, including electrical, fire, and heavy-material-handling risks; compliance with ISO 45001:2018 remains critical, especially for green building projects.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- PEB demand is driven by rising investment in manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, data centres, industrial parks and infrastructure development.
- The industrial sector (automobiles, cement, oil & gas and other core industries) remains the anchor for PEB adoption, while infrastructure applications — warehouses, cold storage, data centres, power plants, aircraft hangars, railway infrastructure — are emerging as the market's next significant growth frontier.
- Organised players hold a structural advantage over the unorganised segment in executing large-scale, time-sensitive projects, reinforcing the case for scaled, integrated manufacturers.
- Steel is increasingly becoming the preferred construction material worldwide owing to its strength, speed of construction, sustainability and cost efficiency.
- Government initiatives — PLI schemes, Make in India, semiconductor manufacturing, renewable energy, electric vehicles, battery manufacturing and data-centre development — are expected to generate significant demand for PEB and structural-steel solutions.
- FY26 revenue growth was driven by rising demand, an improving project mix with a greater share of high-value industrial and manufacturing projects, and execution capability enabled by the expanded manufacturing footprint.
- Rising demand is being seen from leading domestic and global corporations for marquee projects in renewable energy, solar power and data centres, which management expects to remain key growth drivers in the years ahead.
- Closed FY 2025-26 with an order book exceeding INR 1,552 crore.
- Executed the largest single Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) order in the Company's history during FY26.
- Secured major new orders during FY26 from marquee customers including Ather, Ascendas, Rungta Mines, Tata Jaguar, Tecno Data Centre, Takenaka, World Green Energy, JSW JFE, Indo Asia Copper, Bhuwaneshwari Foods & Beverages and CESC Green Power, many partnering with the Company for the first time.

The Company also commenced construction of two strategically important projects: a new PEB manufacturing facility in Gujarat (its first production base in Western India, targeting the Gujarat/Maharashtra markets) and a Heavy Steel Structures (HSS) manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh. Gujarat Phase I commenced operations in July 2026 and Phase II is expected to be completed before December 2026; land has already been acquired for a sixth, fully integrated Gujarat plant expected to begin production by FY 2027-28. other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] "Total Order book as on 31st July 2026, is INR 1,864 Cr", with "Order Wins (Rs in Crs) 609" for "Orders booked between 01st May 2026 and 31st July 2026" and a "major order worth Rs. 165 crore in Gujarat" secured during the quarter. The order-book pie prints 30% and 70% against an "Industrial / Infrastructure" legend, but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from the extract, so the split is not asserted here.
- [JV] Joint Venture Agreement with ER Steel Inc, Canada — Interarch 76% / ER Steel 24% — "to establish a structured framework for jointly evaluating the design, engineering, manufacturing and supply of OWSJ products through a scalable and cost-efficient platform in India". Interarch leads engineering, detailing, manufacturing and quality compliance from India; ER Steel supports market development and sales in USA & Canada.
- [JV terms] "Total funding required by the JV company to procure land, to undertake the development and operationalization of the Business is expected to be INR 80 Crs", and "ER Steel must enter into 100% Offtake Agreement with the JV Co and purchase the total quantity of OWSJ products for distribution and sale in Canada & USA. This is a major commercial assurance for the JV."
- [Export tie-up] Collaboration with Mold-Tek Technologies Limited (MTTL): Interarch handles manufacturing and logistics while MTTL provides detailing for PEB and structural steel projects; a "two-year business plan, extendable by mutual consent", exclusivity "on projects introduced by MTTL", and Interarch pays MTTL "a commission on export orders generated through MTTL's efforts".
- [Export certifications] "Certificate for Inspection Program for Manufacturer of Metal Building System issued by IAS used to supply the pre-engineered buildings in USA" and an "International Code Council – Certificate issued to supply LGFS products in the USA".
- [Name change / one-off] The company is "Formerly known as Interarch Building Products Limited"; FY26 carries an Exceptional Item of -3.2 footnoted as a "One time statutory impact of new Labour Codes".

growth verticals / optionality: Heavy structure capacity (Andhra) unlocking non-industrial bids; 100% export JV in India for North American open web joists (MoU signed, plant by Aug/Sep 2027); expansion of Gujarat plant to 60,000 tons by Dec 2027; potential entry into solar rooftops and modular hospitals
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin held at 9.3% despite Rs.5.5cr one-off costs (export certifications, labor code compliance, outsourced high-rise engineering); steel price volatility managed via dynamic bidding; no margin erosion despite Q4 steel price rise due to forward pricing discipline
capex / expansion: Rs.1,000cr+ total planned (FY26-28); Rs.500cr+ deployed in FY26; Gujarat PEB plant (Phase-1: July 2026, Phase-2: Dec 2026); Andhra heavy structure plant (Phase-1: July 2026, Phase-2/3: FY28); land bank secured for future expansion
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (80%+); dividend recommended at 125% of face value (Rs.12.5/share); no buybacks mentioned; JV funding for export unit to be equity-funded
risks & watch-items: Labor migration volatility (seasonal/election-linked); steel price spikes (managed but not eliminated); execution risk in new heavy structure segment; JV partner dependency for export market access; regulatory delays in project clearances
management quality / tone: Highly confident, proactive, and execution-focused; emphasized preparedness over opportunism; clear roadmap for capacity and segment expansion; dismissed margin pressure concerns with pricing discipline; tone suggests market leadership ambition
non-obvious takeaways: Rs.102cr order for Rajpath government building signals entry into high-profile public infrastructure; JV for North American joists is a strategic pivot to capture export demand with zero domestic competition; labor disruption in March was election-linked, not structural; heavy structure plant enables entry into stadiums, airports, and high-rises — a $50bn+ TAM beyond traditional PEB
